title: Validity evidence for the Clinic Screening Tool for HIV (CST-HIV) addressing factors that undermine health-related quality of life in people living with HIV.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the psychometric properties and clinical validity of the Clinic Screening Tool for HIV (CST-HIV) to determine whether the CST-HIV demonstrates a reliable multidimensional structure and clinically meaningful associations with established patient-reported outcome measures (PROM) and HIV clinical markers.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted within the Spanish CoRIS multicentre cohort, including 286 adults with HIV. Participants completed the CST-HIV and validated PROMs. Clinical indicators (CD4 cell count and percentage, HIV-1 RNA viral load, and non-AIDS events) were collected at current and retrospective time points. Analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency, convergent and discriminant validity, associations with clinical markers, and age-group comparisons.
RESULTS: Confirmatory factor analysis showed good model fit, with satisfactory internal consistency across domains (ω = 0.86-0.89). CST-HIV shows convergent validity, including psychological distress with PHQ-4 ( = 0.79), anticipated stigma with HIV stigma ( = 0.65), sexuality with sexual satisfaction ( = -0.74), sleep and fatigue with insomnia severity ( = 0.79), and material deprivation with social exclusion ( = 0.67) (all < 0.001). Anticipated stigma (ρ = -0.16, = 0.014) and material deprivation (ρ = -0.18, = 0.005) were associated with lower CD4 counts, while material deprivation was associated with higher viral load (ρ = 0.13, = 0.046). Sexual satisfaction was lower among participants aged ≥50 years ( = -0.47, < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The CST-HIV demonstrates strong psychometric performance, supporting its use as a valid, brief, multidimensional screening tool to inform person-centered HIV care and clinical intervention.
